chapters.title: Introduction: Why this isn't a poker book
chapters.sourcePressure: The opening contract uses Pete Carroll's Super Bowl XLIX pass and the poker-versus-chess contrast to separate process quality from outcome quality under uncertainty, luck, and hidden information.
chapters.coreMove: Reconstruct the live decision before letting the final outcome judge it.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating uncertainty as an excuse for failed choices instead of a demand for better process reconstruction.
mustNotDriftInto: excusing bad process because luck exists

chapters.title: Life is poker, not chess
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter makes poker the governing model for real decisions because information stays hidden and luck can separate a sound process from a single result.
chapters.coreMove: Commit under incomplete information while describing confidence as a range, not a verdict.
chapters.commonMisread: Assuming poker means randomness dominates, so judgment and accountability become softer.

chapters.title: Wanna bet?
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter turns confident claims into priced beliefs so the gap between tone and real conviction becomes visible.
chapters.coreMove: Make a belief name its price before treating its confidence as real.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning bet language into a dare, dominance move, or literal gambling recommendation.

chapters.title: Bet to learn: fielding the unfolding future
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter treats outcomes as staged feedback from an unfolding future, requiring proportional updates rather than snap verdicts or reactive swings.
chapters.coreMove: Move confidence only as far as the new evidence earns.
chapters.commonMisread: Calling every new result a lesson and wobbling with each noisy data point.

chapters.title: The buddy system
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter shows why solo review bends around ego and why a trusted challenger can test assumptions, confidence, and after-the-fact rewrites.
chapters.coreMove: Invite a trusted challenger to audit the story before ego edits it clean.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the buddy as a comfort provider, mentor, or automatic cheerleader.

chapters.title: Dissent to win
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter scales truth-seeking from one buddy to group culture, using dissent and CUDOS-style norms to keep consensus from impersonating evidence.
chapters.coreMove: Give the strongest objection a protected place before the group locks its choice.
chapters.commonMisread: Equating useful dissent with loud contrarianism, combat, or endless objection.

chapters.title: Adventures in mental time travel
chapters.sourcePressure: The source support is thinner here, so the plan stays narrow: mental time travel widens present judgment through future review, 10-10-10 thinking, premortems, backcasting, and regret placed before commitment.
chapters.coreMove: Let a future review point inspect today before the present mood spends the chips.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating future perspective as prediction, manifestation, or clean foresight.
